subject: Post-demo recap + prioritized eval plan (Finlytics)
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Sam Wilson <sam.wilson@finlytics.com>, Priya Rao <priya@finlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap + prioritized eval plan (Finlytics)

Hi Sam / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap from our side and a proposed, prioritized set of tests so we can quickly validate migration risk and cost/latency tradeoffs versus the hyperscaler you mentioned. I attached a compact test matrix (XLSX) and a tiny smoke script for API compatibility.

Key takeaways from the call:
- Primary goal: replace current hyperscaler setup for document extraction + reranking while keeping prompt fidelity and improving 95th/99th latency tails.
- Constraints: Finlytics needs OpenAI-API compatibility for minimal app changes, ability to run in a dedicated-reserved pool, and predictable per-token economics for budgeting.
- Security: data residency in us-east-1, audit logs, and SOC2 artifacts required for procurement.

Why Redwood is a fit (short):
- OpenAI-compatible surface (same request/response shapes, API keys) to minimize SDK churn.
- Routing + fallback: can pin to dedicated capacity and fail over to hosted variants with no client changes.
- Observable unit economics: token-level breakdown in Console + per-route latency buckets for spike analysis.

Proposed prioritized test plan (high level):
1) Smoke (compat) — run a small set of production prompts through our OpenAI-compatible endpoint to check syntax/semantic parity and identify prompt diffs.
2) Perf (latency/throughput) — run side-by-side against your hyperscaler baseline (95/99 percentile and tail behavior).
3) Regression (output quality) — sampling-based prompt diff comparisons across your usual prompt set and a few adversarial prompts.

Please confirm the priority order above and whether we should run the smoke test against a copy of your current deployment or a sample dataset. If you sign off, we’ll schedule the smoke run early next week and share exact commands + URLs to collect results.

Attachments: redwood-finlytics-eval-matrix-20270405.xlsx (test matrix), api-compat-smoke-script.sh (tiny reproducible smoke script)

Thanks —
Rachel Kim
Head of Solutions (Americas)
Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0142
From: Sam Wilson <sam.wilson@finlytics.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@finlytics.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + prioritized eval plan (Finlytics)

Thanks Rachel — great summary. Quick responses and a few asks from our side before you start tests: 

1) Priorities: we agree with the order (smoke -> perf -> regression). Our procurement lead wants an initial compatibility signal first.

2) Smoke scope: please run the smoke script against a small set of prompts we rely on (attached as prompts_sample.txt). Key success criteria are: no schema changes required for the client, and top-5 responses must not diverge on intent for >80% of prompts.

3) Perf baselines: we’ll provide telemetry for our current hyperscaler baseline (avg/95/99). Can you confirm whether Redwood’s perf runs will measure end-to-end latency from our client or just the Redwood runtime? We’d prefer E2E to capture network and routing.

4) SDK swap: timeline question — if we need to swap SDKs from the hyperscaler client to your OpenAI-compatible SDK, how long do you estimate and will we get a shim to minimize changes?

5) Security: we’ll need SOC2 docs and an indication of where audit logs live (Console vs. customer-managed S3).

Can we aim to run the smoke test early Wednesday morning (US Eastern)? I’ll send the sample prompts and a small S3 test bucket link separately.

—Sam
Sam Wilson
Head of Engineering
Finlytics
sam.wilson@finlytics.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sam Wilson <sam.wilson@finlytics.com>, Priya Rao <priya@finlytics.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + prioritized eval plan (Finlytics)

On Tue, Apr 6, 2027 at 09:18 AM Sam Wilson <sam.wilson@finlytics.com> wrote:
> Thanks Rachel — great summary. Quick responses and a few asks from our side before you start tests:
>
> 1) Priorities: we agree with the order (smoke -> perf -> regression). Our procurement lead wants an initial compatibility signal first.

Thanks Sam — we’ll own the smoke run and provide clear pass/fail criteria. A few clarifications and our proposed commitments: 

- Smoke run (owner: Rachel / Ben): we’ll execute your supplied prompts against our OpenAI-compatible endpoint with an identical request payload to your current client (same headers, model key, and body). We’ll capture both raw responses and token-level logs.
- E2E vs runtime-only: we can do both. For E2E we’ll run the client-side request from a controlled Finlytics-like network (we’ll ask for a short-lived tunnel or run from a Finlytics bastion). Runtime-only runs will isolate the serving tail and help diagnose kernel/quantization deltas.
- SDK swap: our OpenAI-compatible surface is intentionally minimal; we can provide a 2-file shim that maps your existing client calls to our endpoint. Small teams have completed the minimal change in <2 hours; larger app wiring varies. We’ll include the shim in the repo we share.
- SOC2 & audit logs: attaching the SOC2 snapshot (redacted) and linking Console audit docs — logs can be sent to customer-managed S3 or kept in Console for faster access.

Immediate next steps I propose: 
1) Finlytics: share sample prompts (you said you would) and a short-lived S3 bucket or link for artifacts; also confirm a time slot for Wednesday 09:00 ET for smoke.
2) Redwood: Rachel and I run smoke, deliver a 1-page compatibility summary within 6 hours of completion containing prompt diffs and any guidance for prompt rewriting.
3) Marissa to run perf harness once smoke passes — expected timeline: perf runs start Thursday US-West and finish by EOD Friday.

Attachments: redwood-soc2-snapshot-redacted.pdf (attached to internal copy), redwood-api-shim.patch

Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Sam Wilson <sam.wilson@finlytics.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@finlytics.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Apr 2027 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + prioritized eval plan (Finlytics)

Dropping in with the perf plan and what I need from Finlytics to run side-by-side comparisons.

Planned perf matrix (short):
- Tests: 1) single-request latency distribution (avg/95/99), 2) sustained throughput (tokens/sec) with 8 concurrent clients, 3) cold-start and kv-cache warmup profile.
- Models: run against your baseline model name + our comparable family (we’ll match param/quantization where possible).
- Metrics collected: client-side E2E (from your bastion) + server-side runtime (kernel-time, batch sizes, queue wait).

What I need from Finlytics:
- Short-lived API key and the endpoint you want mirrored (or we’ll provide a shim and run the client from our test runner if you prefer).
- Sample prompt corpus (already requested) + 3 representative large docs for long-context tests.
- Hyperscaler baseline traces (optional but helpful) — if you can share 95/99 numbers that speeds validation.

Timeline: I can start the perf harness Thursday 04/08 (PST) and finish by Friday 04/09 EOD PST if smoke passes today. I’ll publish a perf report to the Drive folder above with graphs and a succinct recommendation (switch / hybrid / more testing).

Security note: please do not share production keys in-thread. We’ll provide a secure upload link (signed URL) or can accept keys via your secrets manager’s temporary token.

Marissa Cole
Performance Engineering
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

--
Marissa attached: link to perf harness (internal) and the command template to run load: ./run_load.sh --prompts prompts_sample.txt --concurrency 8 --duration 300
